footer.privacy: Your data stays in your browser and the sync location you choose. This site collects no data.

home.intro: Maintain one agent-neutral list of permission rules and MCP servers, and generate configuration for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity, and more. Everything runs in your browser.

tools.title: Set up tools
tools.summary: Manage command tools and built-in tools in one place, and flag high-risk tools.

mcp.title: Set up MCP servers
mcp.summary: All agents share one list. Each server automatically becomes an MCP tool.

rules.title: Write permission rules
rules.summary: Allow, ask, or deny by tool and pattern. Conflicts and high-risk rules are flagged automatically.

output.title: Generate output
output.summary: Generate each agent's configuration by scope, then copy and paste it.

rules.title: Permission rules
rules.description: Write allow, ask, and deny rules for command tools, MCP tools, and built-in tools.

mcp.description: Maintain the MCP servers you connect, with content in Claude-style JSON.

presets.title: Presets
presets.hint: Presets are the initial content that ships with the site. When the site updates its presets, you can merge in the new entries or reset everything.
presets.mergeHint: Adds only entries that aren't in your workspace yet. Your changes aren't overwritten.
presets.mergedNone: All preset entries are already in your workspace. Nothing was added.
presets.skippedHint: They have the same names as entries already in your workspace. If needed, change the keys of the existing entries and merge again.

skipped.tag: Tag {{key}}: A tag with this key already exists. New tools use the existing tag instead.
skipped.command_tool: Command tool {{key}}: A command tool with this key already exists.
skipped.mcp_server: MCP server {{key}}: An MCP server with this key already exists.
skipped.agent: Agent {{key}}: An agent with this name already exists.
skipped.built_in_tool: Built-in tool {{key}} of {{agent}}: This agent already has a built-in tool with this key.
skipped.rule: Permission rule {{tool}} {{pattern}}: Its tool was skipped.

presets.resetHint: Replaces your whole workspace with the presets. Everything you added or changed is lost.
presets.resetDescription: All tags, tools, MCP servers, agents, and permission rules in your workspace are replaced with the presets. You can't undo this. To keep them, export your workspace first.

gist.title: Gist sync
gist.hint: Sync your workspace manually across devices through your own GitHub gist. Pushing and pulling overwrite everything; changes on both sides aren't merged.
gist.tokenGuide: You need a token with gist access only. For a classic token, select only gist. For a fine-grained token, set Gists to Read and write under Account permissions.
gist.secretWarning: A secret gist isn't encrypted. It doesn't appear in public lists or search results, but anyone with the link can see it. Don't put secrets in your workspace.
gist.localOnly: Your token and gist ID are saved only in this browser. They aren't part of your workspace or export files.
gist.tokenHint: You need a token to push. To pull only, you can leave it empty.
gist.gistIdPlaceholder: Leave empty to create one on your first push
gist.gistIdHint: To pull on another device, enter the same ID or gist URL there.
gist.gistIdInvalid: Couldn't recognize the gist ID. Enter the ID itself or the URL of the gist page.

token.missing: No token set. Enter one before you push.

gist.missing: No gist linked. One is created on your first push.
gist.invalid: The gist ID isn't valid. Change it in Authentication.

gist.created: Created a secret gist and pushed to it. The gist ID is saved.
gist.pulled: Pulled the workspace from the gist.
gist.invalidStructure: The token and gist ID saved in this browser weren't valid and were cleared. Enter them again.
gist.description: agent-weave workspace (created by agent-weave to sync across devices)
gist.confirmPushTitle: Overwrite the gist with your local workspace?
gist.confirmPushDescription: agent-weave.jsonc in the gist is replaced entirely by your local workspace. Nothing is merged.
gist.confirmPullTitle: Replace your local workspace with the one in the gist?
gist.confirmPullDescription: Everything in your local workspace is replaced. You can't undo this. To keep it, export a backup first.
gist.remoteNewer: The remote is newer than your local copy. Pushing overwrites the newer remote changes.
gist.localNewer: Your local copy is newer than the remote. Pulling discards the newer local changes.

tools.commandToolsHint:
- A command tool is a program that the agent runs through its shell.
- All agents share command tools.
tools.keyHint: The command itself. In a permission rule's pattern, enter only the command prefix that follows it.
tools.deleteWithRules_one: {{count}} permission rule points to it and is also deleted.
tools.deleteWithRules_other: {{count}} permission rules point to it and are also deleted.
tools.deleteNoRules: No permission rules point to it.

mcp.serversHint:
- Each MCP server automatically becomes an MCP tool, so you can write permission rules for it directly.
- All agents share MCP servers.
mcp.keyHint: The server name in the output.
mcp.contentHint: A Claude-style JSON object, such as `command`, `args`, and `env`. Only checks that it's a JSON object; you're responsible for the fields. Environment variable placeholders like `${VAR}` are output as is, so keep secrets in local environment variables.
mcp.descriptionHint: Shown only in this tool. Not included in the output.
mcp.deleteWithRules_one: {{count}} permission rule points to it and is also deleted.
mcp.deleteWithRules_other: {{count}} permission rules point to it and are also deleted.
mcp.deleteNoRules: No permission rules point to it.

rules.noTools: No tools yet. Add command tools on the Tools page, MCP servers on the MCP servers page, or built-in tools on the Agents page.
rules.mcpPatternPlaceholder: For example, query-docs. Leave empty for the whole server.
rules.mcpPatternHint:
- Enter the name of a tool that this MCP server provides, such as `resolve-library-id`.
- `*` isn't escaped. Each agent treats it as a wildcard by its own rules.
rules.patternPlaceholder: For example, push --force. Leave empty for the whole tool.
rules.patternHint:
- Enter the part after the command. It matches by prefix.
- For example, with tool `git` and pattern `push`, it matches every command that starts with `git push`.
- `*` isn't escaped. Each agent treats it as a wildcard by its own rules.
rules.builtInPatternPlaceholder: For example, ./src/. Leave empty for the whole tool.
rules.builtInPatternHint:
- For a path, enter a directory that ends with `/`, such as `./src/`. The template adds the glob.
- `*` isn't escaped. Each agent treats it as a wildcard by its own rules.
- This rule belongs only to {{agent}}.
rules.listHint:
- Sorted automatically by tool type (command tool, MCP tool, built-in tool), tool key, and pattern.
- Rules for the same tool are grouped. The group header shows the tool's description and tags.
- A rule's description appears to the left of its decision. It's for people only and isn't included in the output.
- The output follows the order of the list.
rules.showForTool: View permission rules for this tool

output.noPermission: This agent doesn't output permissions. To turn it on, go to Permission output on the Agents page.
output.copyHint: Copy copies only the {{key}} key and its value, so you can fold the existing property in your editor and replace it. Copy inner copies only the elements of the decision array, so you can append them to an existing array and remove duplicates yourself.
output.skippedRulesHint: This agent definition can't express these rules, so they aren't in the output.
output.noMcp: This agent doesn't output MCP. To turn it on, go to MCP output on the Agents page.
output.mcpCopyHint: Copy copies only the {{key}} key and its value, so you can replace the existing property. Copy inner copies only each server's key and value, so you can add them to an existing object. Remove servers with the same name yourself.
output.mcpTomlCopyHint: Copy copies a set of TOML tables that you can append to the end of the configuration file. If the file already has a table for a server with the same name, delete the old table first.
output.tomlFieldSkippedHint: These field values (such as `null`) can't be written as TOML, so they aren't in the output.
output.placeholderUnexpandedHint: `{{home}}` or `{{user}}` stays as is in the output (rules: {{rules}}, MCP servers: {{servers}}) because your device settings are incomplete.

deviceSettings.title: Device settings
deviceSettings.hint: In the output, `{{home}}` and `{{user}}` in rule patterns and MCP server content expand according to these settings. Device settings are saved only in this browser. They aren't part of your workspace or export files and aren't synced, so the same workspace generates the right paths on each system.
deviceSettings.osHint: Placeholders expand for the selected system. Each system keeps its own username, so you don't need to retype it when you switch.
deviceSettings.userNameHint: The username you sign in to {{os}} with: the last segment of your home directory `{{home}}`.
deviceSettings.incomplete: Placeholders expand only after you select an operating system and enter its username. Until then, they stay as is in the output, and the Output page shows a notice.
deviceSettings.claudePathHint:
- For Claude Code path rules, write paths with `~/`. In its rules, a single leading `/` means relative to the settings file's directory, so the absolute path that `{{home}}` expands to has the wrong meaning.
- `{{home}}` works well in Antigravity rules and MCP server content.
deviceSettings.invalidStructure: The device settings saved in this browser weren't valid and were cleared. Enter them again.

workspaceFile.title: Import and export
workspaceFile.hint: Save your whole workspace as a JSONC file to back it up or share it with colleagues. You can add comments to it in an editor. You can also replace your current workspace with such a file.
workspaceFile.exportHint: Export files don't include your gist token, gist ID, or device settings.
workspaceFile.confirmDescription: Everything in your current workspace is replaced. You can't undo this. To keep it, export a backup first.
workspaceFile.summary: The file contains command tools: {{commands}}, MCP servers: {{servers}}, agents: {{agents}}, permission rules: {{rules}}. Last modified {{updatedAt}}.

pwa.updateDescription: Refresh to apply it. Your workspace is saved automatically, but anything you're entering and haven't submitted is lost, so you can finish first and then refresh.

agents.addHint: Enter the basic information to create the agent. You can add the permission output and MCP output on the Agents page later.
agents.name: Name
agents.permissionOutputHint: When this is off, the agent doesn't output permissions or list skipped rules.
agents.scopesHint: Only tells you which file to paste the output into. Doesn't affect the output.
agents.mcpOutputHint: When this is off, the agent doesn't output MCP.
agents.mcpStyleHint:
- **JSON**: Writes the servers into the object at the property path, such as `mcpServers`.
- **TOML**: Generates a table for each server, such as `[mcp_servers.github]`.
agents.mcpPropertyPathHint: A dot-separated path, such as `mcpServers` or `mcp_servers`.
agents.propertyPathHint: A dot-separated path, such as `permissions` or `userSettings.globalPermissionGrants`.
agents.decisionKeysHint: The key for each decision in the output. Leave it empty if the agent doesn't support that decision; rules with that decision become skipped rules.
agents.deleteDescription: Its built-in tools ({{tools}}) and the permission rules that point to them ({{rules}}) are also deleted. Shared rules aren't affected.

templateHelp.commandWith:
Used when a rule has a pattern.

- Available placeholders: `{command}`, `{pattern}`.
- For example, with `Bash({command} {pattern} *)`, `git` with pattern `push` becomes `Bash(git push *)`.
- If it's empty, rules with a pattern become skipped rules.
templateHelp.commandWithout:
Used when a rule omits the pattern to cover the whole tool.

- Available placeholder: `{command}`.
- For example, with `Bash({command} *)`, `git` becomes `Bash(git *)`.
- If it's empty, rules without a pattern become skipped rules.
templateHelp.mcpWith:
Used when a rule has a pattern. The pattern is the name of a tool that the MCP server provides.

- Available placeholders: `{server}`, `{pattern}`.
- For example, with `mcp__{server}__{pattern}`, `github` with pattern `create_issue` becomes `mcp__github__create_issue`.
- If it's empty, rules with a pattern become skipped rules.
templateHelp.mcpWithout:
Used when a rule omits the pattern to cover the whole MCP server.

- Available placeholder: `{server}`.
- For example, with `mcp__{server}`, `github` becomes `mcp__github`.
- If it's empty, rules without a pattern become skipped rules.
templateHelp.builtInWith:
Used when a rule has a pattern. A path pattern is a directory prefix that ends with `/`, and the template completes the glob.

- Available placeholder: `{pattern}`.
- For example, with `Read({pattern}**)`, pattern `./src/` becomes `Read(./src/**)`. Another example is `read_file({pattern})`.
- If it's empty, rules with a pattern become skipped rules.
templateHelp.builtInWithout:
Used when a rule omits the pattern to cover the whole tool. No placeholder is needed.

- For example, `Read` or `read_file(*)`.
- If it's empty, rules without a pattern become skipped rules.

builtInTools.title: Built-in tools
builtInTools.keyHint: Unique among the built-in tools of {{agent}}. Permission rules that point to it belong only to {{agent}}.
builtInTools.writesHint: A tool that writes files. Allowing it to write anywhere, to the root directory, or to the home directory creates a high-risk notice.

tags.listHint:
- Sorted by key.
- Deleting a tag doesn't change the tools that have it. Those tools keep the reference, which appears as a deleted tag with a warning icon.
tags.keyHint: Unique among all tags. Tools refer to tags by internal ID, so changing the key or name doesn't affect tags already applied.
tags.name: Name
tags.nameHint: Shown in tool lists and filters.

showTools.command: View command tools with this tag on the Tools page
showTools.mcp: View MCP servers with this tag on the MCP servers page

tags.deleteWithTools_one: {{count}} tool has this tag. After you delete it, the tool keeps the reference, which appears as a deleted tag with a warning icon. You can remove it when you edit the tool.
tags.deleteWithTools_other: {{count}} tools have this tag. After you delete it, those tools keep the reference, which appears as a deleted tag with a warning icon. You can remove it when you edit each tool.
tags.fieldHint: You can select more than one. Tags are only for grouping and filtering and don't affect output.
tags.fieldDanglingHint: Tags with a warning icon have been deleted. Clear them to remove them.
tags.fieldEmpty: No tags yet. You can add them on the Tags page.
tags.dangling: This tag has been deleted. What you see is a leftover reference.

notices.highRiskReasonPlaceholder: Why it's high risk (optional), for example: can't be recovered after deletion
notices.toolHighRiskHint: Allowing a rule that points to it creates a high-risk notice.
notices.ruleHighRiskHint: Creates a high-risk notice when the decision is Allow, even if its tool isn't high risk.
notices.highRiskRule: High risk: allows a high-risk operation
notices.conflictRule: Conflict: the same tool and pattern have another decision
notices.highRiskDetail: These rules allow high-risk operations: their tool or the rule itself is flagged as high risk, or they allow a built-in tool that writes files to write anywhere, to the root directory, or to the home directory. This is only a reminder and doesn't affect the output.
notices.conflictDetail: The rules in each group have the same tool and pattern but different decisions. Each decision is output as usual; which one takes effect depends on the agent's own precedence.
